newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel says to watch economy on tax hike - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel says to watch economy on tax hike - Jiji.

text.p: The chairman of the government's tax research council, Hiroshi Kato, said on Tuesday that Japan's planned consumption tax increase can be implemented as planned in April, 1997, if economic conditions remain as they are, Jiji news agency reported.

"If the economy stands as is, we can implement the tax hike as initially planned. However, we would like to keep watch over economic movements until April in carrying out this plan," Kato was quoted as telling reporters after meeting the heads of other government panels handling fiscal and admistrative reforms.
Japanese cabinet ministers have agreed to increase the consumption tax to five percent from the current three percent from next April.
The three panel chiefs basically agreed that the consumption tax hike should be implemented as planned, the Jiji report said.

Jiji also quoted Kato as saying that Japan has yet to decide whether to continue special income tax cuts introduced to boost the economy. If Japan was to continue special income tax cuts, the government may have to issue deficit-financing bonds, he added.
